To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
elevated root nicotian- amine concentrations are critical for hyperaccumulation across different edaphic environments and that this is independent from soil Zn availability.
elevated nicotainmine concentrations in roots of Arabidopsis hallei are critical for Zn accumulation in a range of soils differing in Zn availability.
the expression of the nicotianamine synthase gene AhNAS2 is important for Zn hyperaccumlation across diverse soils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a key factor for Zn hyperaccumlation in a metallophyte that thrives across a wide range of edaphic conditions.

the question whether the same set of mechanisms conferring Zn hyperaccumulation to A. hallericrosses diverse edaphic conditions, and we show that the constitutively expressed metal chelator AhNAS2 plays a key role in this respect.

the identification of a common set of factors that confer hyperaccumulation across different soils and thus contributes to a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying the ability of A. hallei to thrive across an extremely broad range of metalliferic and nonmetalliferic environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AhNAS2 is a Zn hyperaccumulator gene in A. halleric.
AhNAS2 is a Zn hyperaccumulator factor, but not a Zn stress response factor.
the AhNAS2 gene is a Zn hyperaccumulator gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AhNAS2 is a Zn hyperaccumulator gene that is expressed constitutively in all habitats of A. hallei, and that this is the reason for the species-wide Zn hyperaccumulation.
the metal hyperaccumulation phenotype of this species is not a plastic response, but a genetically fixed feature.
AhNAS2 is an A. halleria-specific Zn hyperaccumulation gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the importance of the AhNAS2 gene for the hyperaccumulation of Zn is conserved across a wide range of soils, including those with high Zn concentrations.
the same set of mechanisms is responsible for Zn hyperaccumulating in different soils, and that the same mechanisms are also responsible for Cd, Mn, Co, and Ni accumulation.
the same mechanism can contribute to Zn hyperaccumulators’ success across a broad range of metalliferrous and nonmetallifereous environments.
